acceptance_criteria.criterion: After the fix, calling a wrapped tool with no arguments results in both project_path and cwd_path set to the injected project path
Calling a wrapped tool with an explicit cwd_path value strips the caller-supplied value and re-injects the authoritative project path as cwd_path
Calling a wrapped tool with an explicit project_path preserves that value (setdefault semantics) while still injecting cwd_path
The same injection behaviour applies to both flat-dict and ToolCall nested-dict (input['args']) invocation structures
Module-level docstring and inline comments are updated to reflect that both parameters are now injected

summary: Replaced the delete-then-setdefault pattern with dual injection in _wrapped_ainvoke. project_path uses setdefault (preserves explicit caller values); cwd_path is always force-set to the authoritative _proj value, overwriting any caller-supplied cwd_path. Both the flat-dict and ToolCall nested-dict branches are covered. Updated module-level docstring, inject_project_path function docstring, and inline comments to reflect dual injection semantics."

comments.note: No observations — code is clean and consistent with existing style.

summary: Ran 31 targeted tests in TestDualInjection (AC1–AC4) plus 427 regression tests across the full suite. All 458 tests pass (1 skipped — live MCP). Zero failures, zero regressions.
AC1 verified: empty flat-dict and ToolCall inputs receive both project_path and cwd_path set to the authoritative project path.
AC2 verified: caller-supplied cwd_path in both flat-dict and ToolCall structures is overwritten; project_path also injected.
AC3 verified: explicit caller project_path is preserved via setdefault semantics; cwd_path is still force-set to the authoritative path.
AC4 verified: flat-dict and ToolCall nested-dict (input['args']) invocation paths produce identical injection results (TestDualInjection::test_ac4 + TestToolCallDictStructure).

AC5 verified: module-level docstring (line 5), design-notes section (lines 23–24), inject_project_path function docstring (lines 43, 60), and inline comments (lines 100–103) all reference the dual-injection behaviour.

comments.note: No test covers list/tuple input types (only str and None are covered in TestNonDictPassthrough). Both are forwarded correctly by the isinstance(input, dict) guard, but explicit tests would harden this contract. Low priority — the guard is trivially correct.
Pre-existing aiosqlite/asyncio event-loop teardown warnings on Python 3.14 (test_graph.py, test_integration.py) are unrelated to this change and were present before.

summary: Code review PASS. The dual-injection implementation in tool_wrappers.py is clean, correct, and well-architected. The closure-with-default-argument idiom is idiomatic Python that correctly avoids the late-binding pitfall in loops. The object.__setattr__ bypass for Pydantic v2 is the right technique. Asymmetric semantics (setdefault for project_path, force-set for cwd_path) are clearly documented at every level — module docstring, function docstring, and inline comments. The ToolCall branch detection heuristic is informal but safe in practice. Test coverage is thorough: 11 test classes covering injection, preservation, idempotency, Pydantic compatibility, ToolCall structure, and all four AC scenarios. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: The ToolCall detection heuristic ('args' in input and isinstance(input['args'], dict)) could theoretically misfire on a flat-dict tool call that happens to contain a key named 'args' with a dict value. No real MCP tool argument is named 'args', so this is safe in practice, but the assumption is implicit. A short comment on line 89 acknowledging the heuristic would make the constraint explicit for future maintainers.

[documentation-forward] The Context section (line 31-35) references 'WP-005' as the test origin. This is now superseded by WP-001, which extended the test suite with TestDualInjection. The docstring could be updated to note that dual-injection tests were added in WP-001 so the history is traceable.

notes: All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met via code inspection and QA pipeline results (458/458 tests passing). One documentation-forward item: update the Context section in tool_wrappers.py to reference WP-001 alongside WP-005 for the dual-injection test additions. No blocking issues.
